**Run a revised Q1 pilot. Defer Q2’s full comparison and adoption decision.** Q1 addresses a live path the release smoke never exercised. Q2 can still test fault detection, but its present corpus, oracle and stopping rule would not establish that the added duty improves ShipLoop.

I reviewed `origin/main` at `6dd6d12e3d3cad8346b6d3c6af446d59607d8d08`, both earlier Astra reviews, E1–E9, relevant commit messages, runtime code and retained case records. No files were changed or live samples launched.

**Q1 is worth running; I would narrow it and add one real continuation.**

Keep the two-case pilot with four fresh samples per case. Choose contrasting cases: one small retained prefix and one longer prefix or shared-command correction. Expand according to distinct failure mechanisms and copying difficulty; three permission-assignment cases provide limited additional coverage.

Add one local continuation through amended test-spec, resumed implementation, testing, document and commit. Assert that:

- The original completed actions and commits remain selected.
- Every cursor resumes at the unfinished step.
- Interrupted dirty edits remain in that step’s change.
- Frozen cases, review-added tests, open items and count floors survive.
- The required final regression runs.

A step-plan-only replay cannot establish those downstream properties. Frozen-case preservation is enforced later, at test-spec. [shiploop_navigator.py — `_frozen_case_refusal`:3061](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:3061)

If copying proves troublesome, test a prefilled immutable prefix or mechanical assembly **before submission**. Preserve the submitted canonical result and its replay identity. The shipped implementation’s decision against silently inserting rows was specifically about conflicting producer replays; it does not rule out preparing the draft mechanically. [shiploop_navigator.py — `apply`, replay equality:4423](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:4423)

**Q2 needs a narrower claim and better cases before its cost is justified.**

The nominal seven-fault/seven-control design costs **84 document samples**. Most historical faults concern initial Proof construction, classification or tool availability. Finding them at document would demonstrate another opportunity to catch planning errors. It would not demonstrate that observations from the completed step changed what should happen next.

Fix-forward also changes the economics. A later failure now preserves the earlier completed steps. An earlier document send-back still prevents the current step from becoming completed and sends that step through the cycle again. Earlier diagnosis could avoid downstream work, but the replay does not measure that benefit against the current-step repetition. `_commit_stage` runs only after accepted `document/done`, following its review. [shiploop_navigator.py — `_commit_stage`:3358](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:3358)

I would:

- Keep representative old faults as a **secondary historical diagnostic**, with duplicates grouped by mechanism.
- Add cases where decisive information first becomes available during the preceding step: an observed interface mismatch, fixture-lifecycle fact or changed dependency assumption.
- Add matched controls with the consequential fault removed, including harmless new observations that should leave the plan intact.
- Require successful repair/continuation on promising cases before adoption.
- Treat a positive document-only result as justification for piloting the deferred “document done plus amendment request” route. It cannot validate that unimplemented route.

Two findings qualify the premise that the new refusals already cover the old failures.

First, the repeat-safety addition is **feedback after a Proof fails**, not a plan-time repeat-safety detector. Successful same-tree Proof receipts can be reused. Commit `be98fb8e94c1d0310e3ee39953090620acb6fb07` explicitly declined running every Proof twice because of its cost. [shiploop_test_loop.py — `step_proof`:1638](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_test_loop.py:1638), [failure feedback and `REPEAT_LINE`:1695](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_test_loop.py:1695)

Second, **the focused-search refusal misses p0-terra’s exact historical command**. Its quoted docstrings contain semicolons. `search_only` splits at those semicolons without respecting shell quoting, interpreting `throws` as another program:

```text
suite=focused
segment-leading words=['rg', 'throws', 'rg', 'throws']
search_only=False
check_confirms=PASS
```

That was reproduced with an in-memory probe against the retained plan. Add this exact command as a regression case and address the classifier separately before classifying p0 as prevented by the shipped gate. [Historical p0 command:160](/Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/20261030/p0-terra-ask-agent-55bfcd/.shiploop-runs/seed/run/results/nav-49a22f541c1b4ca4af8b7e062965166d.md:160), [shiploop_test_layers.py — `search_only`:123](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_test_layers.py:123)

**The measures are partly script-decidable, but the registered decision rules need these corrections.**

| Registered measure or rule | Problem | Concrete replacement |
|---|---|---|
| First `check` passes fix-forward | CLI check stops at the first failing gate. Several gates precede fix-forward. Absence of its refusal does not establish that it ran. | Preserve the first submitted draft and score canonical row fidelity separately from whole-check success. |
| Direct `_fix_forward_refusal` result | It returns `None` for malformed steps, leaving rejection to the shape gate. It also checks more than copying. | Require valid shape, `outcome: done`, and an independently verified nonempty retained prefix. Report copying, marks, remaining-work and criterion-ownership failures separately. |
| Stage accepted within its loop | The stage-suite runner counts a producer parked at Improve as accepted. Accepted results can also have outcome `blocked`. | Separate producer completion, pending review, and final accepted `done`. Run through Improve if final acceptance is the endpoint. |
| Failing step’s row changed | Change does not establish repair; valid repairs need not change that row. | Use a registered per-case correction predicate over the relevant fields, followed by an executable behavioral check where possible. |
| Number of refusals | The trace’s standard refusal counter explicitly excludes failed `check` calls. | Report failed checks, rejected completions and distinct revised drafts separately, scoped to the sampled action. |
| Q2 hit names step ID and token | Quoting the bad command or mentioning it while proposing an invalid repair can earn a hit. Valid alternative wording can miss. | Either label this a lexical diagnostic, or use calibrated case-specific predicates that check the proposed correction and preserved obligations. |
| “Recorded amendment” at document | Its representation and effect are unspecified. Document cannot submit `steps`; that field belongs to step-plan. | Define the exact artifact and grammar being scored. Distinguish a proposal from an accepted plan amendment. |
| Any intervention on a clean boundary is a false alarm | Absence of a later historical send-back does not establish that the boundary is fault-free. | Validate controls prospectively; otherwise report an intervention rate on controls. |
| T hits two more fault cases | Three samples per arm leave “case hit” undefined. | Freeze an aggregation rule, such as at least two of three samples, and report every sample plus paired case wins/losses. |

The relevant acceptance behavior is explicit: `accepted_reached` stops at Improve; `seeded_result` returns the parked producer result; `grade_sample` treats any such result as accepted. Under the default planning-review policy, an item’s prior send-back triggers amendment review. [stage_live.py — `accepted_reached` and `seeded_result`:149](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/test/shiploop_e2e/stage_suite/stage_live.py:149), [stage_live.py — `grade_sample`:647](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/test/shiploop_e2e/stage_suite/stage_live.py:647), [navigator — `_first_item_review`:510](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:510)

Keep producer and final reviewed artifacts separately. `finish_improve` rechecks fix-forward, but Improve import has its own gate list rather than rerunning `_evaluate` wholesale. [navigator — `finish_improve`:4465](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:4465), [Improve import gates:10192](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:10192)

The historical p0 amendment demonstrates the row-change problem directly: its `steps` are unchanged; the relevant repair changes the shared search command from `focused` to `check`. Gym demonstrates the other direction: changing the plan to diagnosis does not establish that the runtime fault is fixed. [p0 amended command:166](/Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/20261030/p0-terra-ask-agent-55bfcd/.shiploop-runs/seed/run/results/nav-22ffe6e240574302801b29bbc993400a.md:166), [earlier fix-forward review — gym analysis](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/docs/experiments/step-boundary-replan-20261112/astra-fix-forward.md)

There is also an evidence-capture gap. **The check record is overwritten by each check.** The trace records exit and refusal information, but not the submitted draft. A final export cannot reliably recover first-draft fidelity. Archive each checked draft, its answer and relevant state identity at submission time. Preserve failed checks separately from `trace.refused`, which deliberately excludes them. [shiploop_check.py — `answer_path`:33](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_check.py:33), [shiploop_trace.py — `record_command`:170](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_trace.py:170), [`refused`:415](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_trace.py:415)

The script can decide structural invariants, recorded outcomes, counts and calibrated executable predicates. **The existing data cannot settle arbitrary amendment quality, preserved requirement meaning, remote correctness, production false-alarm rates or net savings.** Those require narrower executable contracts, additional observations or explicitly qualified interpretation. A token oracle cannot supply those judgments.

Before sampling, freeze the entire case manifest, treatment wording, scorer, aggregation, deadlines and missing-data/retry policy. Register tokens for all cases before the first sample, rather than allowing later cases to adapt to earlier outputs. If the pilot changes the packet or apparatus, keep that pilot separate from the revised experiment.

The 70% first-check prediction and 50% change threshold are not inherently contradictory, but they create an explicit **50–69% “keep despite missed prediction” band**. State why that friction is acceptable. Likewise, a sub-90% completion rate does not by itself identify copying as the cause; environment failures or unrelated gates should not automatically trigger mechanical row insertion.

**Faithful reconstruction requires the information and execution boundary, not just the plan and completed file changes.**

| Material | What must be preserved |
|---|---|
| Request and authority | Original requirement intent, item context, dependencies, relevant owner decisions and the run guard. The `osascript` case changes meaning if its original prohibition disappears. |
| Knowledge home | Boundary-time `spec.md`, `architecture.md` and `environment.md`, including requirement IDs, command classifications, harness readiness, fixture lifecycle and platform facts. |
| Accepted records | The plan and complete test spec in force, plus relevant earlier implement/test/document results, assumptions, resolutions and review-added tests. Preserve amendment ancestry where applicable. |
| Pending observations | Q1 needs the recorded send-back and the evidence it actually had. Q2 must exclude that future send-back, subsequent repairs and future knowledge. |
| Repository state | Correct committed frontier, current-step code/tests, interrupted dirty changes, deletions, modes and relevant ignored/generated prerequisites. |
| Bases and receipts | Lint base, preparatory-base relationship, step review base, iteration ledger and the test records needed by counts and registrations. |
| Runtime configuration | Planning-review mode, delegation route, selected Improve card and dependencies, shipped package identity, guard/tool configuration and the registered model/effort. |

The neutral seed home is insufficient for historical replay: it supplies one synthetic `R-1` and a basic command list. Both sampled stages read all three living knowledge files. [run.py — `seed_home`:1301](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/test/shiploop_e2e/run.py:1301), [shiploop_knowledge_home.py — `READS`:115](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_knowledge_home.py:115)

Similarly, generic synthetic summaries erase open obligations, while synthetic `test/done` results do not automatically supply the separate test-run records used by cumulative counts. Verify `open_items`, registered tests and accepted counts against expected reconstructed values. [shiploop_assumptions.py — `open_items`:187](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_assumptions.py:187), [shiploop_test_loop.py — `registered`:431](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_test_loop.py:431), [`accepted_counts`:1066](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_test_loop.py:1066)

Two temporal distinctions are especially important:

- **For Q1**, retain the unfinished step’s dirty edits. Proof-input checks inspect the current checkout, while expectation checks use the lint base; reconstructing only completed commits changes the problem presented to the planner.
- **For Q2**, the target step’s final commit is too late to serve directly as its pre-document snapshot. That commit includes document and Improve edits. Use a retained pre-document snapshot where available; otherwise disclose the reconstruction gap. [navigator — `_check_proof_inputs`:2976](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:2976), [`_commit_stage`:3358](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:3358)

New run IDs, action IDs, paths, timestamps, Git commit identities and explicitly synthetic setup receipts are acceptable. Keep a provenance map and consistent references. Copy boundary-appropriate evidence into the fixture and rewrite locators; leaving absolute references into the original completed run permits hindsight leakage.

The clean-case selection also needs clarification. My read-only scan of the eight source states found **no wholly send-back-free multi-step items**. The additional send-back-free items are single-step. If “clean” means a post-amendment boundary in a formerly faulty item, say so: those controls already contain remedial knowledge. Otherwise draw controls from the wider corpus or construct paired corrected fixtures. [late.out — source-run manifest](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/docs/experiments/step-boundary-replan-20261112/late.out)

**`seed_route` is a useful apparatus extension, provided it preserves real transition effects and checks their results.**

The existing seam is the right foundation: it applies synthetic results, finishes synthetic reviews and calls `accept_effects` with the original pre-transition state. That function deliberately runs effects without running gates. Consequently, reaching a boundary establishes a constructed state, not that the historical plan would pass today’s gates. [stage_build.py — `SEAM_SEED_SCRIPT`:589](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/test/shiploop_e2e/stage_suite/stage_build.py:589), [navigator — `accept_effects`:10058](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:10058)

I would require these safeguards:

1. **Assert each entry’s expected item, stage and step.** Repeated stage names are insufficient. Assert the final action and regenerate `seeded.stage`, `seeded.action` and `settled` from the final state.

2. **Apply each overlay immediately before its owning result, after prior effects finish.** If S2’s files arrive before S1’s document completion, S1 can commit them or absorb them into S2’s baseline.

3. **Replay file changes rather than cherry-picking historical step commits mid-route.** Synthetic document acceptance creates real commits. Moving HEAD independently can violate the iteration ledger’s expected base. Compare file/tree contents and preserve original hashes as provenance.

4. **Represent deletions and modes explicitly.** The present `copytree(..., dirs_exist_ok=True)` overlay is additive. It cannot faithfully replay deletion. The existing implementation-replay representation already distinguishes `files` and `deleted`. [stage_build.py — `lay`:611](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/test/shiploop_e2e/stage_suite/stage_build.py:611), [run.py — `seed_run`, implementation input:1348](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/test/shiploop_e2e/run.py:1348)

5. **Validate all bases and the ledger.** The step-entry review snapshot, recaptured lint base and iteration HEAD serve different purposes. A send-back deliberately preserves the lint base so pending edits remain visible. Assert commit contents, ledger ownership and absence of a new execution for retained steps. [navigator — `_transition`:4722](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:4722), [`_iteration_base`:4747](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:4747), [`_iteration_entry`:3271](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:3271)

6. **Handle automatic advancement explicitly.** Entering validate-existing executes actual shell checks and can settle the stage. Entering document can generate N/A, potentially starting Improve. The latter happens inside effects, after the seed’s earlier synthetic-review completion. Detect these transitions; do not consume the next route result against the wrong action. [navigator — `_validate_existing_entry`:4831](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:4831), [`_document_entry`:4865](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:4865)

7. **Preserve N/A eligibility.** A document boundary settled automatically has no document-model treatment opportunity. Do not add a dummy code change to force one. The live runner already refuses script-settled targets. [stage_live.py — `run_sample`:778](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/test/shiploop_e2e/stage_suite/stage_live.py:778)

The statement “Salesforce cases need no org because neither stage deploys” is therefore too strong. Setup can execute expectation commands; document duties include running changed examples; step-plan asks for tool and harness revalidation. Audit those dependencies per fixture. An artifact-only reconstruction can be useful, but its acceptance claim must remain limited to that environment. [shiploop_prompts.py — step-plan duties:1307](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_prompts.py:1307), [document duties:1549](/Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_prompts.py:1549)

Before live sampling, calibrate two positive route fixtures—late send-back and pre-document—and negative fixtures for wrong-stage entries, misplaced overlays, missing retained obligations and automatic N/A. Calibrate the scorer against correct repairs, cosmetic changes, token-only mentions and requirement-weakening alternatives.

**The proposed sample sizes support a development screen, with much weaker conclusions than the percentages suggest.**

First specify whether Q1 thresholds apply per case or to pooled samples. If pooled, the registered arithmetic is:

| Q1 sample set | Accepted samples needed for ≥90% | First-check passes needed for ≥70% prediction | First-check passes sufficient to avoid the <50% change trigger |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Two-case pilot, 8 samples | 8 | 6 | 4 |
| Seven cases, 28 samples | 26 | 20 | 14 |
| Eight cases, 32 samples | 29 | 23 | 16 |

These rules are arithmetically decidable once outcomes, exclusions and denominators are fixed. They are unstable as reliability estimates. Even under an optimistic independent-binomial model:

- **8/8 successes** gives a one-sided 95% lower bound of approximately **68.8%**.
- **29/32 successes**, which satisfies the registered acceptance rule, gives approximately **77.5%**.
- A process with true 90% success passes the eight-sample requirement of 8/8 only **43%** of the time.

Those are exact-binomial calculations, not valid population guarantees for this selected, heterogeneous corpus. [NIST — exact binomial confidence limits](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman2/auxillar/exacbino.htm)

For Q2, three samples make a majority rule possible, but “any hit,” “two of three” and “all three” measure materially different behavior. Freeze one. With seven clean cases, T has 21 clean samples: even **zero** alarms leaves an illustrative one-sided 95% upper bound of **13.3%**; **one** alarm leaves **20.7%**. Two extra case hits can also come from repeated instances of the same permission-assignment mechanism.

Keep Terra 6.1/xhigh as registered, use fresh isolated sessions, and interleave B/T within cases so execution time and environment drift do not align with treatment. Report per-case outcomes and mechanism-level results alongside pooled totals. This follows the ordinary rationale for blocking comparable experimental conditions. [NIST — randomized block designs](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pri/section3/pri332.htm)

I would use the existing sample budget to find concrete failure modes and select the next experiment. A broader adoption claim should wait for calibrated scoring, genuinely new-information cases, successful continuations and measured action/token/time costs.
